description: Width tiers for Languages — Y7-10 Second Language Entry pathway, Year 9-10 band. All standards are capability descriptors (EC = communicating; EU = understanding). EC strand standards use task_contexts as the primary width axis. EU strand standards use phenomena_contexts (Language and Culture) or mixed (Systems of Language).
subject: Languages

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest task context or phenomenon that honestly satisfies the descriptor's command term at Y9-10. For EC strand: minimum is the narrowest context in which the described communicative act is genuine — not scripted or modelled repetition. For EU strand: minimum is engagement with the described language feature or concept in at least one familiar context with evidence of understanding beyond recognition.
width_notes.typical_width: The full descriptor scope at Y9-10 — grounded in the most common elaboration cases and building from Y7-8 prior learning. For EC strand: a range of task types and communicative contexts that demonstrate the increased independence, complexity and cultural scope the Y9-10 descriptors require. For EU strand: the range of language features, comparisons and analytical moves described in the elaborations.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add new communicative contexts, cultural communities, task types or analytical frameworks. Width adds breadth of context and transferability — not difficulty of the same task. For EU strand: additional phenomena, cross-linguistic comparisons or intercultural contexts that deepen understanding without exceeding the year band.
width_notes.elaborations: Spanish (Y7-10 Second Language Entry sequence) elaborations were used as the primary source. All target-language-specific examples have been genericised. Elaborations are preserved verbatim in each standard entry as source record.

AC9LS10EC01.minimum_width: Initiate and sustain at least one interaction in the target language in a familiar context, exchanging ideas or opinions with a peer using active listening and at least one conversation maintenance strategy.
AC9LS10EC01.typical_width: Initiate and sustain interactions in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts to exchange ideas, opinions and personal experiences — using strategies for conversation maintenance (active listening, follow-up questions, spontaneous responses, repair). Discuss topics of personal and social relevance. Compare and share experiences across cultural contexts.
wider: Interact in a semi-formal or unfamiliar context (e.g. with an older speaker, in a simulated professional context) using appropriate register and repair strategies
Discuss a contentious personal or social topic where opinions are likely to diverge — manage differing views with appropriate discussion strategies
Share and compare experiences across cultural contexts with a target language community member or simulation — identify where cultural assumptions differ
elaborations: initiating conversations with peers, family and others using appropriate expressions
expressing, comparing and explaining likes, dislikes and preferences
interviewing other teenagers to build relationships and share views on aspects of young people's lives
developing non-verbal and spoken techniques and strategies to maintain the flow and authenticity of conversations
sharing impressions of past experiences and significant events
discussing personal views on topics such as bullying, beauty ideals and music
using appropriate discussion strategies such as active listening, showing interest, acknowledging others' opinions, responding to and inviting contributions

AC9LS10EC02.minimum_width: Express and briefly justify at least one opinion on a topic of current or social interest in the target language; respond to a counter-argument with a reasoned reply.
AC9LS10EC02.typical_width: Use the target language to question, offer opinions and compare and discuss ideas — expressing and justifying positions, identifying pros/cons and limitations, participating in structured discussion or debate. Use persuasion language and rhetorical strategies. Engage with topics of current or social relevance.
wider: Participate in a formal debate on a current issue in the target language — argue an assigned position and respond to counter-arguments
Compose a short opinion text (letter, post, spoken statement) for a real or simulated audience on a topic of personal or social relevance
Compare media representations of the same topic across target language and Australian English sources — identify where framing and language choices differ and discuss why
elaborations: participating in class discussions or activities to express opinions and reflect on those of others
expressing thoughts about the pros, cons and limitations of ideas and issues raised regarding a given topic
participating in debates about current issues of interest, using language of persuasion and suggesting possible solutions
using slogans and rhetorical devices to support arguments

AC9LS10EC03.minimum_width: Participate in a multi-stage collaborative planning task in the target language, using spoken or written exchanges to propose, negotiate and reflect on at least two stages of the process.
AC9LS10EC03.typical_width: Use non-verbal, spoken and written exchanges to discuss, plan and reflect on activities, events and experiences — including multi-stage planning, negotiating disagreements, managing real or simulated events, and post-activity reflection. Integrate digital communication tools where available.
wider: Plan and execute a real or simulated event using the target language as the primary medium throughout — from planning to post-event evaluation
Maintain a reflective journal or digital record in the target language across a unit of work — trace developing language and cultural understanding over time
Reflect on the experience of using the target language in a real or near-real context — identify what was possible and what was beyond current capacity
elaborations: planning and producing resources such as websites, posters or online features about issues related to the target language speaking world
emailing, messaging or using secure online applications to chat about and reflect on previously planned experiences
planning and playing a game of charades and reflecting on the importance of non-verbal communication and gestures to make meaning
discussing and negotiating a resolution to a common problem
organising, planning and completing all the stages of preparation for an event

AC9LS10EC04.minimum_width: Interpret key information and at least one expressed perspective from a target language text not previously encountered; produce a response that demonstrates awareness of the cultural context or intended audience of the text.
AC9LS10EC04.typical_width: Interpret information, ideas and perspectives from a wide range of spoken, written and multimodal target language texts — travel/cultural texts, informative/persuasive texts, contemporary digital texts, imaginative texts, First Nations Australian contexts. Distinguish fact from opinion. Produce responses appropriate to cultural context, purpose and audience.
wider: Compare coverage of the same event or topic across two or more target language sources — identify differences in framing, emphasis and omission and discuss what drives them
Adapt a target language text for a significantly different audience — discuss the choices required and evaluate the result
Respond to a First Nations Australian text presented in or alongside the target language — reflect on what is conveyed or transformed in the cross-cultural encounter
elaborations: reading tourist brochures and travel websites about diverse locations in target language speaking communities
obtaining information about a festival, experience, event or tourist site and writing a series of postcards
accessing a range of texts on travel to target language speaking countries and writing a checklist
listening to or reading First Nations Australians' stories in English and creating a profile in the target language
watching a documentary on global issues and summarising the data
analysing and comparing information obtained from a range of sources on topics of social and cultural interest
identifying different perspectives in texts such as articles, reports or blogs, by distinguishing between facts and opinions
gathering information from a range of sources including personal commentaries by target language speaking peers and adults
responding to imaginative texts by modifying key elements
researching, presenting and taking a position on issues relating to contemporary topics

AC9LS10EC05.minimum_width: Identify and explain at least one target language expression that requires cultural knowledge to translate accurately; evaluate a digital translation of a short familiar text and identify at least two limitations.
AC9LS10EC05.typical_width: Apply a range of interpretation and translation strategies in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts — identifying culturally embedded meaning, evaluating translation tools, managing communication challenges. Analyse what is 'lost in translation'. Develop strategies to resolve communication breakdowns. Identify formality levels and adjust appropriately.
wider: Research a concept embedded in the target language that has no direct English equivalent — explain the cultural or social context that gives it meaning
Compare multiple translation approaches (dictionary, automated, peer, self) for the same text — develop a principled framework for choosing an appropriate tool
Translate a text for a real purpose (e.g. a bilingual community resource) — document translation decisions and challenges
elaborations: translating words or expressions that reflect culturally embedded references and concepts
analysing target language translations of familiar English language texts, identifying aspects that got 'lost in translation'
developing personal tools to resolve communication challenges such as rephrasing, asking for clarification or using non-verbal strategies
expanding awareness of false friends by recognising that cognate words may have diverged in meaning
identifying challenges associated with the translation of simple texts
evaluating the effectiveness and risks associated with online translation tools
identifying levels of formality in spoken and written texts and considering what these convey about social relationships

AC9LS10EC06.minimum_width: Create one spoken or written target language text for a clearly identified audience, where at least two language or structural choices are explicitly made with reference to that audience.
AC9LS10EC06.typical_width: Create spoken, written and multimodal texts (informative and imaginative) for familiar and some unfamiliar contexts and purposes — selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and textual conventions to engage different audiences. Produce texts across multiple formats (presentations, narratives, promotional texts, performance texts, collaborative writing). Make deliberate creative choices.
wider: Create the same content for two significantly different audiences — compare the language choices required for each and evaluate the result
Experiment with creative and rhetorical devices from target language literary or oral traditions — discuss their cultural resonance and effect
Produce a real-audience text (bilingual community resource, promotional text, performance) and evaluate its effectiveness based on actual or simulated reception
elaborations: working collaboratively to create a brochure to identify aspects of their city/town/region likely to be of interest to target language speaking visitors
creating promotional and informative bilingual texts to promote events or to support activities
presenting a personal or shared perspective on topics such as fashion, music, cinema or social media
writing a journal entry or contributing to a school newsletter reflecting on the impact of a visit to a significant cultural site
selecting images and using them as creative prompts for target language writing
adapting familiar stories or fictional characters by creating new situations or different effects
composing performance texts such as skits, raps or poems to amuse, entertain and engage learners
composing simplified versions of classic stories for a second language learner audience
experimenting with poetic devices such as rhyme, repetition and onomatopoeia
writing collaboratively — exchanging a text in progress with a peer to write missing sections

AC9LS10EU01.minimum_width: Apply target language phonological features (stress, intonation, vowel/consonant accuracy) with sufficient consistency to be understood in a prepared spoken text.
AC9LS10EU01.typical_width: Apply features of the target language sound system — accurate vowel and consonant production, stress, pitch, rhythm and intonation — in familiar and some unfamiliar spoken contexts. Use phonological knowledge to support pronunciation of unfamiliar words. Understand regional pronunciation variation within the target language. Apply correct terminology for phonological features.
wider: Research and compare pronunciation across two or more regional varieties of the target language — discuss what variation reveals about identity and language change
Analyse the use of pitch, rhythm and intonation in target language audio texts intended for different purposes — identify how prosodic features serve each purpose
Use recording tools to critically review own spoken target language production against a native speaker model — identify specific features to improve
elaborations: recognising the importance of appropriate intonation, stress, tone and pronunciation for making meaning
pronouncing consonants according to vowel combinations and double consonants
understanding variation in pronunciation across the target language speaking world
using the target language pronunciation of letters to spell words and phrases aloud
listening to and reciting texts such as poems, stories, tongue twisters or song lyrics to familiarise with rhythm and intonation
identifying the use of pitch, rhythm, stress and intonation in different audio tracks and how they affect the spoken message

AC9LS10EU02.minimum_width: Apply at least three grammatical structures from the Y9-10 band (e.g. comparatives, a past tense form, cohesive devices) correctly in a target language text.
AC9LS10EU02.typical_width: Select and use a range of target language grammatical structures to enhance meaning — articles and agreement (including nuanced cases), comparatives and superlatives, multiple tense forms (present, past, future), complex sentence construction, cohesive devices, impersonal expressions, adverbs. Apply in spoken, written and multimodal texts.
wider: Investigate how the target language's tense system encodes temporal distinctions that English does not — explain what these differences reveal about how each language conceptualises time
Compare complex sentence construction in the target language and English — identify where the target language requires different syntactic choices for the same meaning
Analyse a native speaker text for grammatical features — identify patterns beyond those explicitly taught and hypothesise about additional conventions
elaborations: knowing when to omit definite and indefinite articles, and adjusting for gender-change cases
using collective nouns and noticing the use of singular verbs
noticing changes in meaning when adjective position changes
using comparatives and superlatives, including some irregular forms
understanding and using indefinite adjectives and pronouns
using possessive and demonstrative pronouns
understanding the use of relative pronouns in familiar contexts
using modelled structures with direct and indirect objects
recognising different past tense forms and comparing uses with English past tense
understanding and using regular and irregular preterite/past forms
understanding and using the immediate future
recognising future and conditional tenses and their conjugational patterns
elaborating on ideas with prepositions
understanding the function of impersonal expressions
using cohesive devices in complex sentences
forming adverbs from adjectives

AC9LS10EU03.minimum_width: Identify and explain how at least two language choices (vocabulary or grammar) in a target language text contribute to its register or effect, using metalanguage.
AC9LS10EU03.typical_width: Reflect on and evaluate target language texts using metalanguage — analysing textual coherence and structure, how language choices create register and effect, the function of cohesive devices, and how language change (globalisation, technology, social media) has influenced the target language. Compare language features across text types.
wider: Research the influence of other languages or cultural contact on target language vocabulary over time — identify specific examples and discuss the mechanisms of language change
Investigate how social media, technology and popular culture have influenced target language usage — identify specific changes and evaluate their significance
Compare how the same content is expressed in formal and informal target language registers — identify all specific language features that signal each register
elaborations: comparing language features of target language and English versions of different types of texts
understanding textual elements that provide coherence at a whole text level
reflecting on how grammatical and vocabulary choices shade meaning and establish register
researching target language words borrowed from different languages across time and through political, historical and social changes
using metalanguage to discuss language structures and features
explaining how language is used differently to achieve different purposes
investigating how social media, globalisation, technology and popular culture have influenced the target language over time

AC9LS10EU04.minimum_width: Explain at least two ways in which specific target language features or practices reflect cultural values or shape identity; reflect on at least one way in which learning the target language has affected own perspectives.
AC9LS10EU04.typical_width: Reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values — in target language communities and own experience. Investigate multilingualism and co-official languages in target language communities. Examine how cultural background and language repertoire affect ways of communicating. Consider how globalisation, migration and popular culture influence language and identity.
wider: Investigate how indigenous languages in target language communities co-exist with the target language — research the history and current status of at least one co-official or community language
Research how a target language community's engagement with globalisation, migration or political change has affected language use and identity — identify specific language changes and their causes
Interview or research a multilingual speaker's experience of identity across languages — document insights and compare with own language learning experience
Examine how First Nations Australian protocols and acknowledgement of Country intersect with target language learning contexts — reflect on own positionality as a language learner
elaborations: recognising that the target language continues to evolve due to exposure to other cultures, globalisation, trends, technology and social change
recognising that many target language speaking countries have indigenous languages that are co-official languages
recognising that the target language co-exists with multiple indigenous languages and dialects in many communities
reflecting on and explaining the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country/Place with a First Nations Australian community
exploring the influence of popular culture in the target language speaking world
considering how regional and national perspectives influence the use of language and sense of identity relating to place/country
interviewing bilingual peers, family members or guests about the experience of using more than one language
discussing ways in which learning a different language can lead to new ways of thinking or interpreting experiences
analysing texts that show different representations of cultural identity and sense of belonging
discussing and reflecting on the nature and role of culture and its expression through language
